overview: White plays c3 to prepare d4 and a big centre while keeping options open. Black often replies 1...e5 or 1...c5 or 1...d5, and the game can transpose to a Slav-like, Ponziani or Sicilian Alapin-like structure. It is rarely played by strong players and can transpose to many things.

white_ideas.idea: Follow with d4 and e4, for a broad centre.
Transpose to Alapin-type or Queen's-Pawn-type structures.

typical_structures.structure: Flexible centre; White c3/d4 against Black e5/d5.

character.notes: Quiet, slightly passive; Black gets an easy game.

soundness.notes: Sound but gives Black comfortable equality.

level.notes: Simple but needs some knowledge of transpositions.

character.reason: Quiet, equalising, neither forcing nor especially hard to break.

structure.reason: A flank opening with an undecided centre.

level.reason: Simple set-up but needs transposition know-how.
